title: Release children inherit unrelated host credentials
reasoning: The release environment begins as a complete copy of os.environ and removes only database/reset credentials and supervisor policy variables. Common credentials such as GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, cloud-provider tokens, and SSH_AUTH_SOCK remain available to supervised children and any repository-controlled commands they launch. CommandRunner forwards the supplied mapping directly to subprocesses.
reproduction: Set GITHUB_TOKEN to a sentinel value, call _release_clawpatch_env(), and run a child that prints whether GITHUB_TOKEN exists; the child receives it.
recommendation: Construct child environments from a minimal operational allowlist. Require explicit opt-in for provider credentials and ensure repository validation or repair commands receive a separately stripped environment.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The environment test verifies removal of DATABASE_URL and a database-reset guard only; it does not seed or reject unrelated credential classes.
suggestedRegressionTest: Seed representative GitHub, cloud, package-registry, and SSH credential variables, run a child through CommandRunner with the release environment, and assert that none are present unless explicitly authorized.
minimumFixScope: Change _release_clawpatch_env and add environment-isolation coverage in tests/test_runner.py.

history.reasoning: The original files still exist, but the evidence changed materially at current local HEAD d6c0a9cbcbbd4128f7c164b5d7d88a2c8cd62ca8. _release_clawpatch_env moved to lines 162-195 and now constructs the child environment from a small operational allowlist instead of copying os.environ. CommandRunner lines 176-180 still forwards an explicitly supplied mapping exactly, which is now safe because release_sweep creates and passes the sanitized mapping. The regression test moved/expanded to tests/test_runner.py:15-54 and now seeds GitHub, AWS, npm, SSH, and database credentials; all three current-source targeted tests passed. The linked attempt's failed pytest used the installed venv package, whose old implementation still inherits SAFE_VALUE, rather than the current source tree; its ruff commands also failed because ruff was absent. The full unittest suite was attempted but the read-only execution environment provided no usable temporary directory, producing 134 tempfile errors rather than a targeted regression. Relevant tracked files are clean. The fix is currently one local commit ahead of origin/main; the untracked .clawpatch state still records the stale failed attempt.
